content.title: Rangers vs. Phillies: Prediction, Lineups, How to Watch (3/28/26)
content.text: The Texas Rangers (0–1) visit the Philadelphia Phillies (1–0) this afternoon, continuing their Opening Week series at Citizens Bank Park. The Phillies took the opener 5–3, powered by a dominant performance from Cristopher Sánchez, who pitched six scoreless innings, allowing just three hits while striking out 10. Kyle Schwarber picked up where he left off after a phenomenal 2025 campaign, putting Philadelphia on board with a two-run homer in the bottom of the first. Alec Bohm provided the rest of the offense with a three-run shot in the bottom of the fifth. The Rangers rallied late, with three runs in the top of the ninth, including two off a homer by Jake Burger. But it was too little, too late. Nate Eovaldi pitched 4.2 innings for Texas, allowing five runs and eight hits — including two home runs — while striking out seven. Jacob Latz makes the start for the Rangers today after Jacob deGrom was scratched due to neck stiffness. Latz had a stellar 2025 campaign, mainly out of the bullpen, with 2.84 ERA in 33 appearances. He made four starts in September, finishing with a 2.01 ERA that month. Aaron Nola takes the mound for the Phillies, looking to rebound after posting a career-worst 6.01 ERA last season, struggling with injuries and command. He gave up 18 home runs in 17 starts. The Rangers have the edge here on the mound. Expect Latz to contain the Phillies’ bats as Nola’s struggles continue in 2026.
